stem: Parth asks whether $62$ can be a perfect square.

options.text: $62$ cannot be a perfect square, because a perfect square cannot end in $2$.
$62$ must be a perfect square, because $6$ is an allowed last digit for some other number.
Decide by running a cube-root check instead of a last-digit square check.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Perfect squares end only in $0$, $1$, $4$, $5$, $6$, or $9$, so a units digit $2$ rules $62$ out.

teacher.key_rationale: Last digit 2 is impossible for a perfect square. B mislabels. C confuses an allowed digit elsewhere with this number. D conflates cube and square tests.
